turns.question: What privacy boundary should "local-only" enforce: must file bytes, metadata, and derived text all stay on this device, including no remote AI processing and no telemetry payload excerpts?

contract.G: Ensure file processing is fully local-only for the primary supported format.
contract.T: Replace remote processing paths for this flow with the on-device parser and block transmission of file bytes, metadata, derived text, and telemetry excerpts off-device.
contract.S: Primary format only; file ingest, parsing, derived-text generation, AI/provider calls for this flow, and telemetry/error reporting that could leak content.
contract.V: Verify the primary-format flow completes without network-dependent processing, confirm no file content/metadata/derived text is sent to remote AI or telemetry, and confirm local parsing still produces expected output.
contract.X: Stop if the flow depends on unsupported formats, if any required processing still needs a remote provider, or if another subsystem outside this flow must also be made local-only.
contract.P: Persist through drafting the smallest verifiable local-only slice for the current file-processing flow; exclude broader privacy hardening outside this path.

turns.question: What refund authority should support have: what amount can they approve directly, and when is owner approval required?
Should support be allowed to issue partial refunds as well as full refunds within that authority limit?

contract.G: Allow support agents to issue customer refunds within defined authority limits.
contract.T: Add refund execution for support agents with full or partial refunds up to $100, require a reason for every refund, route larger refunds to an owner approval path, and record an audit event for refund actions.
contract.S: Support billing permissions, refund action UI/API, reason capture, limit enforcement at $100, owner gate for amounts above $100, full and partial refunds, and audit-event creation.
contract.V: Verify support can issue full and partial refunds up to $100 with a required reason, verify attempts above $100 are blocked or escalated to owner approval, and verify audit records are created for refund actions.
contract.X: Stop if payment-provider constraints prevent these rules, if owner approval workflow requires a broader approvals system not present in this slice, or if non-support roles/policies are requested.
contract.P: Persist on the narrow operational slice needed to let support refund within policy, without expanding into broader billing-role redesign.

turns.question: What retention outcome should this enforce: when should customer uploads be deleted, and are any report artifacts kept?
What recovery semantics should users be told after deletion, given backups can still retain objects for 30 days?

contract.G: Automatically clean up old customer uploads under an explicit retention rule.
contract.T: Delete customer uploads 90 days after their last report finishes, preserve report summaries, and present deletion as final to users even though disaster-recovery backups may age out later.
contract.S: Upload-retention eligibility based on last report completion, deletion job for uploads, preservation of report summaries, and user-facing/account semantics around final deletion versus backup aging.
contract.V: Verify uploads tied to completed reports are deleted only after 90 days from the last report completion, verify report summaries remain available, and verify user-facing messaging states deletion is final.
contract.X: Stop if other report dependencies still require the upload object after the retention point, if backup-policy changes are requested, or if broader data-retention policy work beyond uploads is needed.
contract.P: Persist on the smallest enforceable uploads-retention slice and do not expand into general archival or backup redesign.
